primitives.name: Boltzmann Temperature Recalibration
primitives.verbatim_quote: It cannot tell you whether a measurement was *right* — only that the recorded pieces still add up to the recorded conclusions, so nobody can quietly edit one side.
primitives.assumptions: Data follows a Boltzmann distribution, sufficient calibration samples available, no label noise.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Overconfident models (large β) lead to underdispersion; underconfident models (small β) lead to overdispersion.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI proper scoring rules via exponential family duality; dual variable β corresponds to Lagrange multiplier enforcing probability calibration. In GSE, this is a state-transition kernel for belief update under uncertainty.
layer2.telemetry: Calibration error (Brier score) on held-out test set; cross-entropy loss difference between calibrated and uncalibrated predictions.

primitives.name: Isotonic Regression Post-Processing
primitives.verbatim_quote: It cannot tell you whether a measurement was *right* — only that the recorded pieces still add up to the recorded conclusions, so nobody can quietly edit one side.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'f': 'real-valued function, outputs recalibrated probability', 'y_i': 'binary outcome {0,1}', 'p_i': 'model prediction probability'}
primitives.assumptions: True conditional mean is monotonic in model scores; convex loss quadratic; no ties in sorted predictions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-monotonic underlying relationship causes piecewise constant bias; sparse data regions suffer from step-function artifacts.

layer2.mapping: Isotonically transformed probabilities correspond to conformal predictive intervals under exchangeability. In GSI, this maps to nonconformity measure calibration; in GSE, it enables robust policy evaluation under distribution shift.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error reduction relative to raw model; Kolmogorov-Smirnov test p-value for monotonicity violation after transformation.

primitives.name: Bayesian Shrinkage Prior
primitives.verbatim_quote: # Calibration evidence — what each artifact supports `docs/calibration-proposals/` is the authority for `MODEL_VERSION` bumps, and the JSON in this directory is the measurement those bumps rest on.
primitives.assumptions: Prior belief that predictions should be close to raw model estimates; Gaussian likelihood; conjugate prior for closed-form posterior.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Excessive shrinkage (large σ²) reduces variance but introduces bias; insufficient shrinkage (σ² → 0) recovers original model.

layer2.mapping: Shrinkage induces a weighted average between model and market probabilities, aligning with GSI risk pooling principles. In GSE, this serves as a smoothing transition kernel for policy iteration under uncertainty.
layer2.telemetry: Reduction in Brier score compared to raw model; improvement in log-loss relative to market benchmarks.

reasoning_traces.think:
The three primitives represent distinct routes to recalibrating model outputs. Boltzmann temperature adjusts confidence levels via exponential scaling, maximizing likelihood under a Gibbs distribution. Isotonic regression enforces monotonicity constraints without parametric form, ensuring well-calibrated predictive intervals. Shrinkage priors introduce Bayesian regularization, pulling extreme predictions toward safer anchors (like market consensus). All three methods aim to correct miscalibration—systematic differences between predicted probabilities and empirical frequencies—but operate in complementary regimes: Boltzmann handles over/under-confidence, isotonic addresses non-monotonicity, and shrinkage balances bias-variance. Their coexistence in the calibration pipeline reflects a layered defense against different failure modes, with each method providing independent verification of improvements.
